key_highlights: ASX direction conflicted: Wall Street green and Meta AI model support upside (#5, #16), but oil-driven inflation fears and bond yield spikes pressure the index (#69, #42)
RBA rate hike risk elevated: mortgage stress at 18-year highs (#43), house prices facing potential 10% decline ahead of a fourth hike (#53), Chalmers concedes housing softness (#1)
Property sector stress: Bathla warns of imminent collapse (#78), 'Evergrande moment' for mega developer (#47), fugitive developer dodging ICAC (#68)
Gold sector strong: Auric posts $28M WA profit (#34), Gateway high-grade discovery near Wiluna (#38), King River 44g/t surface sample (#71)
Macro deterioration: productivity 'bad to worse' (#41), per capita recession risk (#72), inflation 'home grown' (#75), economy narrowly avoids recession (#37)
Energy disruption: Hydro Tasmania major power station fire (#17), One Nation coal plant pressure (#24), Chinese solar overtakes coal (#39)
Qantas ground crews vote for strike right (#77); CBA inactive-card fee scandal (#50) dents bank confidence

sectors.trend: Gold names outperform on strong WA discoveries and production; copper and lithium exploration active but early-stage
sectors.implications: Auric (#34), Gateway (#38), King River (#71) support gold miners; True North copper (#31) and ZhongNuo/Chariot lithium (#35) offer speculative upside. Iron ore/coal muted by Chinese solar shift (#39)

sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin compression and reputational risk; rising rates support NIMs but credit deterioration offsets

sectors.trend: Disrupted: Hydro Tasmania fire threatens supply (#17); coal-to-solar transition accelerates (#39); One Nation coal pressure (#24)
sectors.implications: SME.AX, AGL.AX, GPO.AX face supply-risk premiums; coal names (BRL, WDS) under political and structural headwinds

sectors.trend: Severely negative: housing 'bloodbath' forecast (#64), 10% price drop risk (#53), developer implosions (#47, #78), retirement-as-renter crisis (#19)
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) and property developers face devaluation; consumer staples (WES.AX, WOW.AX) benefit from rate-sensitive demand shift

sectors.trend: Mixed: global AI momentum (Meta, Marvell, Citi tech call #51, #54, #66) vs. Iran 'AI bubble' risk (#46); CSL.AX stable; Elevance Health positive (#55, #57)
sectors.implications: ASX tech exposure limited; CSL.AX, SVA.AX defensive; global AI volatility transmits via AUD and risk sentiment

sectors.trend: Qantas strike vote (#77) creates near-term operational risk; Whyalla steelworks uncertainty (#18)
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces industrial disruption risk; BHP.AX steel segment under pressure

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce REIT and property developer exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: 10% house price decline forecast, developer implosions, 18-year mortgage stress highs create systemic property risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim bank exposure pending credit-loss data

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge equity duration with short-duration bonds or cash
defensive_moves.rationale: Global bond yield surge and oil-driven inflation fears create volatility; cash provides optionality

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely volatile and net-negative: rate-hike fears, housing stress, and bond yield spikes outweigh Wall Street green and gold strength. Qantas strike vote adds idiosyncratic risk. Expect ^AXJO to test support levels.
market_outlook.long_term: Productivity deterioration and per-capita recession risk cap upside. Gold and energy-transition metals offer structural support. Housing correction could trigger broader financial-sector stress. RBA policy path is the dominant variable.
